lines.text: Everyone says sugar in a gas tank will destroy an engine so he dumps a quarter cup into a mower.
But watch the jar because the sugar just sinks to the bottom and won't dissolve in gasoline.
Because sugar dissolves in water but gas is an oil so the crystals just sit there like sand in a bucket.
beats: ai:white sugar crystals sitting at the bottom of a glass jar of golden gasoline macro
ai:sand settled at the bottom of a clear bucket of water

lines.text: So the engine fires up and runs for about 105 minutes without dying.
And when he looks inside the tank the sugar is still sitting there.
And the fuel filter catches most of what moves so very little sugar ever reaches the engine.
beats: ai:a small inline fuel filter catching white grains in a clear fuel line macro

lines.text: The compression stays almost the same at 73 psi hot so the engine definitely didn't seize.
But the cylinder head comes out crusty with sugar residue so over time it could still cause trouble.
So is the sugar myth true or not?
